# PR #152 round 4 correctness review

**PASS-WITH-NOTES** at `d8bf33717bff3805fa411d0113864810d99f895a` for the requested producer/consumer reply paths and carried-forward accounting/merge proof. Herring owns the full C32 identity-strength verdict.

## Scope and execution evidence

Reviewed `efa0227eba1fc368038b724e67a03f761b1a3745..d8bf33717bff3805fa411d0113864810d99f895a`: own fix d8bf3371 plus the previously reviewed main import.

Clean pinned checkout; GitHub and ls-remote agree, CLEAN, latest Delivers SUCCESS. CI `42402097818`, attempt 1, matches this head: 2,161 JUnit cases, zero failures/errors. Both Node jobs ran all 113 rust-runtime adapter tests and report 2,247 passed/six skipped overall. New bound-identity, closed-request, verified-pull and OMP-fixture controls, plus retained successful/replay/refused/atomic-answer controls, executed.

No local builds/tests, fixture mutation, daemon/pane probe or live TS-to-daemon run. The three guard mutations are author-reported.

## OMP/Pi reply path repaired

The registered pij_send tool delegates to RustRuntimeSession.send. Its automatic last-inbound correlation now attaches buildCallerContext, including pane/session and process fields, before calling client.send. The same construction covers normal and FYI correlated sends; controls retain their existing caller context. Registration sets PIJ_SESSION_ID to the accepted self id.

The TS test captures the adapter's actual request and compares top-level/caller key sets and populated value types against the shared fixture, independently checking the pane and correlation. A following uncorrelated send has no correlation/caller fields. Fixture values are chosen for the Rust rig, not a claim that both runtimes emit identical literal IDs/PIDs.

The Rust control posts that fixture to /v1/send: without caller it is refused and queues nothing; with caller it binds by pane, queues the expected sender/message once and records one answer. This is the paired wire-shape/Rust-replay proof specified by F106, not assembled live transport evidence.

## Gate and verified-pull mechanics

Known open or closed role-request IDs get the gate; errors reading either table refuse. An ID in neither table retains the explicitly allowed legacy uncorrelated behavior.

Native API calls never supply a VerifiedPull witness. No context or an AssertedId resolution is refused before seat/role/FYI dispatch. A contradictory sender likewise refuses. The normal/FYI and seat/role refusal matrix and closed-row negative/positive ran.

The shim resolves subject_verified once. For a paneless pull it matches native session/host tuple and current process start, then passes an internal VerifiedPull to reply_sender; the sender must match the captured seat. It does not downgrade that witness by resolving the asserted id again. The verified shim positive and identical-caller native negative ran.

The witness is not an accepted wire flag. These checks establish the stated implementation mechanics; whether matching a live registered tuple provides the required registration-strength origin assurance remains herring's security assessment, not this correctness endorsement.

## Other real paths and limits

pij-rs correlated caller forwarding and control-specific forwarding are unchanged; ordinary bound-holder and role/replay accounting controls still pass. The shim's tmux subject path is preserved. The Copilot-native store send implementation is unchanged and currently sends no in_reply_to, so it remains on the pre-existing uncorrelated path rather than being newly refused by this gate.

Answer/audit ownership and semantic acceptance are retained. Schema 0043/SCHEMA_VERSION 43 are unchanged from efa0227, above main's 42 as directed. No new scheduler is introduced; per-correlated-send caller construction and the fallback closed-table lookup are performance-owned.

Uncorrelated raw-from/existence-only identity remains req-10's disclosed work. No claim of universal sender authentication or live cross-runtime proof is made. No producer/consumer regression found in the requested documented scope; no product code was changed by this reviewer.
